subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Edge Cases
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Edge Cases.

hook.text: A self-driving car handles 99 percent of driving beautifully—the remaining 1 percent is terrifying.

buildup.text: Edge cases are rare scenarios that engineers can't fully predict: a mattress on the highway, a costume parade.

discovery.text: Each edge case requires its own solution, and the number of possible weird situations is nearly infinite.

twist.text: A human driver uses common sense to handle the unexpected. No AI system has that kind of flexibility yet.

climax.text: Most self-driving failures happen not in normal driving but in the bizarre moments nobody anticipated.

punchline.text: Self-driving cars fail at the things humans find easy.

quiz.question: What are edge cases in self-driving?

details.summary: Edge cases are rare, unusual situations that self-driving systems struggle to handle, such as a mattress on a highway, an emergency vehicle approaching, or a child chasing a ball into the street.
details.whyItMatters: The long tail of edge cases is the core unsolved problem in autonomous driving. A self-driving car may handle 99.9 percent of situations but that remaining 0.1 percent includes life-or-death scenarios.
takeaways: Edge cases are rare scenarios not well represented in training data
Real-world driving produces an nearly infinite variety of situations
Solving the last one percent of driving scenarios requires enormously more effort than the first 99 percent

faq.question: Can more training data solve the edge case problem?
faq.answer: Data helps but cannot eliminate the problem. By definition, edge cases are rare and diverse. Some situations a car encounters may never have appeared in any training dataset, requiring the system to reason about novelty.

faq.question: What is an example of a real edge case failure?
faq.answer: A Waymo vehicle was confused by a traffic officer manually directing traffic differently from the signals. The car could not reconcile the conflicting instructions and froze, requiring human intervention to proceed.
